Then Thoros became furious against the Greeks,
and he killed more than ten thousand of them.
And the king of Jerusalem came,
and he made peace between the Armenians and the Greeks.
And in the year 1474
1474 of the Greeks [1163 AD],
Qara Arslan, the lord of Hisn Ziyad, attacked Amida,
and he waged a fierce battle against it.
And afterwards, division fell among his forces,
and he abandoned it and left.
And Ya'qub Arslan also entered his territory,
and he captured the fortress of Shumushki (Chemishgezek),
and he took captive about one hundred thousand souls,
and he left the villages laid waste.
Now the bishop Ignatius of Tell Arsenios was taken in captivity as far as Qamakh.
And when he was released,
he came to Melitene.
The bishop of Hisn Ziyad was also captured,
and after two days they released him.
At that time, the wife of the Prince,
he who had been captured and imprisoned in Aleppo,
was quarreling against her son,
and was not willing that he should reign.
And when she was pressured by the nobles,
she sent to the emperor of the Greeks, who was her son-in-law, to come
so that she might deliver Antioch to him.
And when the patriarch and the nobles perceived this,
they sent and brought Thoros from Cilicia.
And he entered Antioch,
and drove the princess {queen} out of the city,
and established her husband {or: son? OCR} in the kingdom.
And in that same year,
which is the year 1448
[or rather 1458
and 55{9?} of the Arabs], Nur al-Din gathered a large army of Turks,
and went and encamped against Hisn al-Akrad (Crac des Chevaliers),
in order to enter and plunder the region of Tripoli.
And on one of the days, at noontime, while the Turkish people were at ease and off-guard in their tents,
the crusaders of the Franks made a sudden assault upon them,
and panic fell upon the Turks.
It is said
that when Nur al-Din saw the standards of the Franks,
he leaped and ran out of his tent in a tunic without a coat,
and mounted his horse, though it was hobbled as was customary.
Then a certain Kurd came and cut the hobbles of the horse,
and Nur al-Din fled and was saved;
but the Franks overtook the Kurd and killed him.
And they put many of the Turks to the sword and took others captive,
and they carried off booty,
and entered Tripoli.
